variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Single-nucleotide deletion causing a frameshift, p.(Pro274HisfsTer13), predicted premature stop 13 codons downstream (from the batch HGVS). Both papers describe the disease mechanism as loss of function; 41741169 places the variant in the OTU domain.

quotes.quote: Haploinsufficiency of A20 (HA20) is a severe childhood-onset inflammatory disease characterized by heterozygous germline loss-of-function (LOF) mutations in TNFAIP3 (1, 2).

A20 haploinsufficiency (HA20) is a monogenic, early-onset autoinflammatory disease caused by loss-of-function variants in the tumour necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 3 (TNFAIP3) gene, which encodes the A20 protein.

concerns: Possible same family across papers: both 39167656 and 41741169 list Boursier Guilaine among the authors (French reference laboratory), and 41741169 Table 3 cites earlier references (12, 46) for this variant, which the converted text does not resolve. Whether 41741169 Family 12 (patient 17) overlaps 39167656 Family-5 (HA20-29/30/31) cannot be determined from the texts; the identities are kept separate by the pipeline.

41741169 says patient 17's carrier parent is asymptomatic and family history is 'Absent', whereas all three Family-5 carriers in 39167656 are listed as individuals with HA20. If the families were the same, these statements would conflict.
39167656 lists the variant only in supplementary Table S1 (no case description, no sex or phenotype for HA20-29).
Transcript: 41741169 uses NM_006290.4; 39167656 states no transcript; the batch uses NM_001270508.2. The cDNA and protein positions as written agree with the batch prediction (protein_check: agrees).

The supplementary pedigree figure of 41741169 (Family 12) is garbled in the converted text; phenotype labels near it cannot be attributed to individuals. The panel may wish to see the original figure.
notes_for_panel: Two sources: a large immune-repertoire study listing a three-carrier family without clinical details (39167656), and a French paediatric cohort with one male carrier whose carrier parent is asymptomatic (41741169). No functional, population or in-silico data in either paper.
